text:
Marathon Petroleum closed essentially flat today, but the stock has climbed 7.8% over the past two weeks as global refinery disruptions tighten fuel supplies and boost margins for U.S. producers. Diesel prices hit record highs this week after Russian and Iranian refineries were knocked offline by military conflict in Ukraine and the Middle East, while the EU joined U.S. sanctions on Iran—shrinking global refining capacity just as U.S. refineries are running at 98% utilization. For a refiner like Marathon, fewer competitors producing fuel means stronger prices for what it does make.

The underlying dynamics remain favorable: U.S. crude sits at $91.50 a barrel while world prices are at $96, giving domestic refiners a cost advantage, and diesel and heating oil inventories are lean at 104 million barrels, leaving little cushion if supply tightens further. The week's geopolitical escalations—including South Korea weighing military involvement to keep the Strait of Hormuz open for oil shipments—suggest energy markets expect sustained supply pressure, which historically supports refiner profitability.
